messages:
sara_support: customer reported a large reserved GPU-hour spike on their April invoice despite low token volumes in us-west. they say most traffic should've hit eu-west pool. attaching their account id and invoice.
ashok_billing: can you paste account ID + invoice line#? I can sanity-check charge mapping and whether SLA credit applied.
sara_support: acct: acct_92Y7Z, invoice: INV-2027-042, line 3. customer says they saw ~120 reserved hours consumed in us-west between 03:10-03:40 UTC. tokens for that window are ~2k only.
lee_sre: odd — low token burn but high hours usually means warmup / idle allocation or cross-region warmup. any routing header overrides from the client? :thinking:
sara_support: customer provided a sample request — they set X-Redwood-Region: eu-west but provider-side logs show route -> us-west. paste below their curl:

devon_prod: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-..." \ 
  -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west" \ 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-large","input":"hi"}'
```

ashok_billing: thanks. forwarding to billing replication. billing-bot, can you surface allocation events for acct_92Y7Z 03:00-04:00 UTC?
billing-bot: allocation-events for acct_92Y7Z 03:00-04:00 UTC:\n- 03:05 us-west reserved-pool-alloc start instance warmup id=alloc-559 (30m)
- 03:07 us-west burst-pool attach id=burst-410
- 03:20 us-west reserved-pool-alloc heartbeat
- 03:38 us-west reserved-pool-alloc terminated
(see /internal/billing/events/alloc-559)
lee_sre: that warmup at 03:05 aligns. is it possible routing policy fell back to us-west because eu-west pool had no spare warm instances? if so warmup would be charged to reserved hours in the region that served the request.
sara_support: customer insists eu-west should have capacity — they have a dedicated pool in eu-west with 0% spare util. i'll ask them for their pool id.
account-manager-elaine: looping me in to keep the customer updated. if this is warmup-fallthrough we may offer provisional SLA credit while we investigate routing policy logs.
devon_prod: quick repro suggestion for eng: hit eu-west header repeatedly with a smaller interval to see if we can trigger route to us-west. also check router logs for header honoring: `/internal/router/logs?acct=acct_92Y7Z&since=03:00&until=03:45`.
lee_sre: i'm pulling router logs now. preliminary grep shows a 03:04 DROP or no-matching-route for the X-Redwood-Region header for that account — fallback policy routed to nearest available pool: us-west. filing an eng task: RWD-6123 investigate header precedence + warmup routing.
ashok_billing: I'll flag for billing review. if eng confirms fallback caused billed reserved hours we can evaluate SLA credit for the 33 reserved hours billed in us-west. keeping customer updated.
sara_support: customer replied: "we didn't change config; please fix and credit if it was your fallback" — they want timeline and a repro. assigning to devon/lee. :eyes:
lee_sre: next steps: 1) eng reproduce with curl and header (devon) 2) confirm router header precedence bug (me) 3) if confirmed, create billing adjustment request referencing INV-2027-042 and alloc-559 (ashok). ETA 24-48h. :white_check_mark:
ashok_billing: noted. I'll prepare provisional credit template in case we can confirm. CCing finance approval path.
sara_support: thanks all — i'll keep the customer posted and add notes to the support ticket: SUP-7409. closing thread here until we have repro/confirm.
